The equation of the line $l_{1}$ is $y = 4x - 7$ and $l_{2}$ is perpendicular to $l_{1}$. What is the equation of $l_{2}$?

$y =$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $4,$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $-\frac{1}{4}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=-\frac{1}{4}$ and a $y$-intercept of $1.$ Therefore, it can be written in slope-intercept form as

$$
y=-\frac{1}{4}x+1.
$$

Let ${l}_{1}$ denote the line $y=-2x,$ and let ${l}_{2}$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $-2,$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $\frac{1}{2}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=\frac{1}{2}$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(12,-2).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-2) & =\frac{1}{2}(x-12) \\ y+2 & =\frac{1}{2}x-6 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}x-8\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Perpendicular Line

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let ${l}_{1}$ denote the line $y=-5x+8,$ and let ${l}_{2}$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $-5,$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $\frac{1}{5}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=\frac{1}{5}$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-10,-5).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-5) & =\frac{1}{5}(x-(-10)) \\ y-(-5) & =\frac{1}{5}(x+10) \\ y+5 & =\frac{1}{5}x+2 \\ y & =\frac{1}{5}x-3\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Perpendicular Line

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let ${l}_{1}$ denote the line $y=\frac{1}{4}x+7,$ and let ${l}_{2}$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $\frac{1}{4},$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $-4.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=-4$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-3,4).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =-4(x-(-3)) \\ y-4 & =-4(x+3) \\ y-4 & =-4x-12 \\ y & =-4x-8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b=-8.$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Perpendicular Line

question.:question/problem: The lines $y=-\frac{1}{5}x+1$ and $y=mx+b$ are perpendicular. Given that the line $y=mx+b$ passes through the point $(-1,-1),$ what is the value of $b?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let ${l}_{1}$ denote the line $y=-\frac{1}{5}x+1,$ and let ${l}_{2}$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $-\frac{1}{5},$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $5.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=5$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-1,-1).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-1) & =5(x-(-1)) \\ y-(-1) & =5(x+1) \\ y+1 & =5x+5 \\ y & =5x+4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b=4.$
